title: task edit can append to every list field except acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone, so adding one criterion requires rewriting the whole list
description:
Found while working QCLI-322 on 2026-09-17, by hitting it rather than by reading the help: sharpening one acceptance criterion on a freshly-filed task required passing the ENTIRE --acceptance-criteria array back, because no append flag exists.

quest task edit carries an --add-* for every other list field: --add-plan, --add-note, --add-label, --add-dependency, --add-assignee, --add-reference, --add-modified-file, --add-comment. For acceptanceCriteria and definitionOfDone it offers only:

  --acceptance-criteria / --definition-of-done   full replacement
  --check-ac / --uncheck-ac / --remove-ac        index-addressed, no append
  --clear-ac / --clear-dod

So these two are the only list fields with remove-but-no-append. There is no --add-ac / --add-dod.

Why this is more than an inconsistency: the index-addressed checkbox flags exist precisely so two editors do not overwrite each other, and the task-execution guide says so in as many words -- "Checkbox edits are index-addressed, so two editors do not overwrite each other ... Prefer them over replacing a whole list." Appending a criterion is the one checklist operation that CANNOT follow that advice. The guide tells a caller to avoid whole-list replacement while the CLI leaves them no alternative, so the concurrent-overwrite hazard the design avoids everywhere else is reachable here by anyone adding a criterion to a live task.

The exposure is real but bounded: --if-revision (QCLI-277) makes the unsafe path detectable, and it is what was used on QCLI-322 rather than an unguarded rewrite. That turns a silent clobber into an exit-5 conflict, which is the difference between a hazard and a defect -- but it makes the caller opt into a precondition to do safely what every neighbouring field does safely by default.

Adjacent to QCLI-283 (create/edit flag-name divergence). That task is about a flag being NAMED differently between create and edit; this one is about an operation being ABSENT on edit entirely, so fixing 283 alone would not produce --add-ac. Filing this task hit QCLI-283 live, incidentally: the first attempt passed --add-dependency, which create rejects in favour of --dependency, and the whole create failed exit 2. Same family, opposite direction to the --label/--reference case already recorded there.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task edit accepts an append for acceptance criteria and definition of done in the same shape as the other list fields, so adding one item does not require passing the existing ones back
Appending does not disturb the positions of existing items, and the checklist-position contract the task-execution guide documents still holds after an append
A test covers appending to a task that already has criteria, asserting both the new item and that the pre-existing items are unchanged in text and position
The task-execution guide no longer advises against whole-list replacement while leaving append as the one operation that requires it
bun run check exits 0 with the new tests included
